fuel_consumption.source_quote: Based on projected 2004 fuel usage, such an increase would result in an increase to aircraft fuel expense of approximately $268 million in 2004, inclusive of the impact of fuel hedge instruments outstanding at December 31, 2003

instrument_type_details.notes: Beginning in March 2003, the Company stopped entering into new hedge contracts and in June 2003 terminated substantially all contracts with maturities beyond March 2004 (collecting ~$41 million in settlements). Commencing October 2003, Company resumed entering into new option contracts only. Instruments use WTI Crude oil and NYMEX Heating oil as proxy commodities. Fair value $54 million at Dec 31, 2003 (vs. $212 million at Dec 31, 2002).

warnings: Hedging program was suspended March-September 2003 due to financial condition; contracts with maturities beyond March 2004 were terminated in June 2003.
Company resumed hedging in October 2003 with option contracts only (no swaps).
Total fuel consumption in gallons not explicitly stated.
12% overall 2004 hedge is approximate blended rate; quarterly breakdown: ~21% Q1, ~16% Q2, ~6% Q3-Q4.
This filing covers AMR Corporation (parent); American Airlines, Inc. (CIK 6201) is the principal operating subsidiary.
Credit rating constraints continue to limit hedging ability.
